parts.label: (i)
parts.text: Describe the distribution of land and land use in Somalia.

parts.label: (ii)
parts.text: Suggest two reasons for the distribution of intensive agriculture in Somalia.

parts.label: (iii)
parts.text:
Intensive agriculture is often commercial.
State what is meant by commercial agriculture.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
The photograph shows a Spodoptera moth.
Spodoptera moths eat plants, including crops such as maize. Lizards eat Spodoptera moths.
Eagles eat lizards. Wolves eat eagles.

parts.label: (i)
parts.text: Construct the food chain containing three trophic levels which includes Spodoptera moths.

parts.label: (ii)
parts.text:
Spodoptera moths are primary consumers.
State what is meant by primary consumer.

parts.label: (iii)
parts.text:
Farmers in Somalia want to control the population of Spodoptera moths. A scientist
has found a fungus that kills Spodoptera moths. The fungus does not exist naturally
in Somalia.
Suggest benefits and limitations of releasing a fungus into Somalia to control the
population of Spodoptera moths.
benefits ______
limitations ______

parts.label: (iv)
parts.text:
A farmer notices that some individual plants in the maize crop are not affected by
Spodoptera moths.
Describe how these plants can be used to produce a maize crop that is resistant to
Spodoptera moths.

parts.label: (i)
parts.text:
A scientist investigates the population of Spodoptera moths in a 1000 m field of maize
using a random sampling technique.
Describe how the scientist:
• uses random sampling
• uses a quadrat
• records the data collected
• obtains an estimate for the population of Spodoptera moths in the field.

parts.label: (ii)
parts.text:
Estimating the population of Spodoptera moths using a quadrat has limitations.
Suggest two limitations of sampling Spodoptera moths using a quadrat.

parts.label: (iii)
parts.text: Suggest one other method for estimating the population of Spodoptera moths.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
In 2022, it was estimated that 2.8 million people in Somalia could not meet their daily food
requirements. One strategy to prevent malnutrition is to provide school children with meals.
Charities, such as the World Food Programme, provide the food for the meals.
Suggest benefits and limitations of this strategy for preventing malnutrition.
benefits ______
limitations ______

parts.label: (c)
parts.text:
The government of Somalia wants to find out if there is a difference in access to safe drinking
water for people in rural areas compared to urban areas.
A questionnaire was used to survey 200 men.
question response
1.
2. Do you have access to safe drinking water?
3. How far do you have to travel to access safe drinking water?

parts.label: (i)
parts.text:
The questionnaire is incomplete and will not allow a conclusion to be made.
Suggest a suitable question that will allow a conclusion to be made.

parts.label: (ii)
parts.text: Suggest two ways to improve the survey.

parts.text: The photograph shows a person collecting water from a shallow well dug in a dry river.

parts.label: (i)
parts.text: State the source of water that is accessed by wells.

parts.label: (ii)
parts.text:
The river is dry because of a drought in Somalia.
Suggest two other reasons why the river is dry.

parts.label: (iii)
parts.text:
Water collected from shallow wells is an important source of fresh water in Somalia.
Describe two limitations of collecting fresh water using the method shown in
the photograph.

parts.label: (e)
parts.text:
Malaria is a disease that kills more than 2000 people a year in Somalia.
Malaria is spread by mosquitoes infected with the malaria parasite. Mosquitoes are the vector
for spreading malaria.
State two strategies of vector control for malaria.

Somalia has deposits of uranium. Mining companies want to extract the uranium.
State three factors that the company must consider before deciding to extract
the uranium.

parts.label: (iii)
parts.text:
Some people are concerned about uranium mining in Somalia.
One local person says:
I live in a village near the mine.
How will the mine affect me?
Suggest how the mine will affect people living in a nearby village.

parts.label: (iv)
parts.text:
The mining company agrees to restore the landscape once the extraction of uranium
is finished.
Describe two strategies to restore the landscape.

parts.text:
Uranium is a nuclear fuel and can be used to generate electricity. In Somalia all of the
extracted uranium is exported.

parts.label: (i)
parts.text:

generate electricity.

parts.text:
A report stated that in 2022, 36% of people in Somalia had access to electricity.
Calculate the number of people in Somalia in 2022 that did not have access to electricity.
